The Child Care Nutrition Enhancement Act sounds compassionate until you follow the money. Increasing reimbursements by $5,700 annually per provider doesn’t solve systemic bloat—it just feeds a broken bureaucracy. Washington’s answer is always more cash injections, never structural reform. 

Why shovel $7,200 per center into the same failed administrative pipelines instead of letting states streamline nutrition programs without federal middlemen? Real solutions would slash red tape choking small providers and redirect existing funds from foreign aid pet projects. 

But no—career politicians would rather throw taxpayer dollars at the problem than fix the root causes.
